text:
jamie: short followup from today's all-hands Q&A on positioning — capturing consensus and next steps.

alex: TL;DR for GTM: lead with customer pain (unpredictable cost + ops), then our three pillars: predictable economics, unified runtime, production controls. keep it <20s.

maria: suggested external one-liner: "Redwood delivers predictable LLM inference: consistent latency, measurable unit costs, and a clear path from hosted to private deployments." feedback?

sam: looks good. add optional tech blurb for eng audiences: "GPU-optimized runtime with continuous batching, KV cache, and quant-friendly paths."

lee: benchmarks to standardize for slides/RFPs: p50 chat latency, p99 tail latency, and $/1M tokens. ops-bot: pin canonical bench URL.

ops-bot: bench dashboard: https://redwood.internal/bench/2025-q4

taylor: from sales: customers ask if we're "another endpoint." answer: start Hosted for speed, migrate to Dedicated/Private for scale, cost predictability, and compliance. highlight the migration path.

jamie: public collateral — use category-level competitor framing; name names only in RFPs with data.

maria: I'll add a migration doc + FAQ to product docs (PR by Friday). includes: when to pick Dedicated vs Private, measuring cost savings, and data residency options.

sam: can we have a 1-page cheat sheet for SEs/engineers on deployment recommendations?

lee: I'll draft the engineer one-pager with heuristics (traffic, compliance, latency goals) and example autoscale config.

alex: i'll draft a canonical external paragraph after syncing with GTM Monday; avoid public numeric claims unless linked to canonical bench.

taylor: i'll collect top 5 sales objections and share with alex/maria.

ops-bot: recording: https://meetings.redwood/ah-2025-11-07

jamie: thanks all 97 i'll assemble slide snippets once PRs are in. feel free to add follow-ups here or DM me.
